key_claims.claim: On the real KBONUS-BKG light curve of KIC 5689121 (45,648 cleaned points), TLS 2.0.1 recovers P = 13.769643 +- 0.0013 d, SDE 105.3, SNR 27.5, depth 1999 ppm, 74 distinct transits, odd/even mismatch 0.21 sigma in 198 s on one thread (100 s with 4 threads); astropy BLS gives P = 13.76953 d, box depth 1649 +- 56 ppm, odd 1634 +- 81 vs even 1662 +- 78 ppm, secondary -71 +- 57 ppm, harmonic_delta_log_likelihood -430.

A batman+emcee fit with supersample_factor=7 and exp_time=1765.464 s gives t0 = BJD 2455630.2454, P = 13.769444 +- 0.000038 d, rp/rs = 0.0443, b = 0.35, a/rs = 43.7, transit-derived stellar density 5.9 (+1.3/-2.6) rho_sun and Rp = 2.45 R_earth (undiluted), in 109 s; LEO-Vetter 1.2.0 flux-level metrics (MES 24.2, 74 transits) raise no FA or FP flag.

Inverted and quarter-scrambled copies of the same light curve, through the identical cleaning and a 499k-period astropy BLS (objective='snr'), reach BLS depth-SNR 9.6-11.9 (global SDE 5.1-6.8) at 19.7-29 d with the longest trial duration, versus SNR 30.3 (SDE 29.3) for the real signal: a BLS SNR of ~10 is a noise-level statistic in a half-million-period Kepler search.
key_claims.source: scratchpad/algorithms-tooling/s07.log and null_throughput.json; consistent with Kuber's first-screen result (31/29 real vs 32/28 inverted) in analysis/kbonus-extension-20261011/README.md and Chopra's 12-25 d pile-up in docs/GUIDE.md

key_claims.claim: wotan paper: optimal biweight window is about 3x the transit duration; w/T14 >= 2.2 preserves >= 98% of the flux integral; discarding half a window at edges is slightly preferable; iterative GPs/splines are inferior to robust sliders for transit searches. Chopra chose 0.75 d by injection-recovery (3/16, 10/16, 8/16, 5/16 recovered for 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5 d); Kuber used 1.0 d per quarter; eumemic uses clip(3*T14(Pmax), 0.5, 1.0) d.

key_claims.claim: Over-detrending measured: with 2000 ppm, 2.3 h transits injected into a 90-d active-star synthetic LC, biweight 1.0 d recovers 1970 ppm, biweight 0.3 d 1443 ppm, cosine 1.0 d 1515 ppm, wotan gp(matern) 1096 ppm; masking the transits and re-detrending at 0.3 d recovers 2176 ppm; celerite2 Matern-3/2 with transits masked recovers 2232 ppm in 0.37 s.

TLS FAQ white-noise SDE/FAP table: SDE 5.7 (1-FAP 0.9), 6.1 (0.95), 7.0 (0.99), 8.3 (0.999), 9.1 (0.9999); the FAQ states the table is optimistic under red noise and SDE > 9 is the conventional threshold; the TLS paper reports 93% vs 76% recovery versus BLS with both at ~1% false positives at SDE ~ 7.

eumemic calibrated false alarms on inverted light curves of 798,769 random full-sky stars: among clean-pixel SNR >= 9 signals 726 real vs 96 expected false alarms; 46% of clean SNR >= 9 signals with MES < 10 are expected to be noise, 16% at MES 10-12, 2% above; injections at nominal SNR 10 are recovered at SNR >= 9 only 22% of the time (48% at >= 7.5); search costs: coherent astropy BLS 17.5 s, stack-slide 8.9 s, semi-coherent 4.2 s per TESS star with recoveries 60/62/52%.

key_claims.claim: KBONUS-BKG light-curve files hold a LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED extension (TIME in BKJD, QUARTER, FLUX = PSF flux, SAP_FLUX, PSF_FLAT_FLUX, SAP_QUALITY, FLATTEN_MASK) plus per-quarter LIGHTCURVE_Q extensions (FLUX = corrected PSF flux, SAP_FLUX, CENTROID_COLUMN/ROW, SAP_BKG, RED_CHI2, PSF_FLUX_NOVA) and APERTURE_Q masks; the primary header carries TPFORG 5689116, KEPMAG 16.332, GMAG 16.282; KIC 5689121 has 13 usable quarters, 46,523 good points and 1,033 ppm per-cadence scatter.
key_claims.source: astropy.io.fits inspection of the downloaded file; https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsp/kbonus-bkg

actionable_steps: Pin the toolchain in /home/user/ZyushgPlanet: lightkurve 2.6.0, astropy 8.0.2, transitleastsquares 2.0.1, wotan 2.0, batman-package 2.5.3, emcee 3.1.6, celerite2 0.3.3, leo-vetter 1.2.0, exovetter 0.0.16, dynesty 3.1.0 (all now in the venv); keep TRICERATOPS (pytransit==2.2 pin) and psfmachine (pandas 1.5.3 pin, needs Python <= 3.11) in separate venvs.

Port eumemic's MIT-licensed fastbls.py (numba _season_scan, _coherent_best, _stackslide) and search.py helpers (period_grid, expected_duration, sde, event_stats, refine) as the batch search engine; use astropy BoxLeastSquares only for the coherent refine step and compute_stats, and TLS 2.0.1 (use_threads=1 inside workers, oversampling_factor 3, TIC limb darkening via catalog_info(TIC_ID=...)) only on survivors.

Never call BoxLeastSquares.autoperiod on multi-year baselines (83.8M periods for Kepler); build the density-aware grid with oversample 3 (512k periods for a 0.5 Msun star over 4 yr) or let TLS build its Ofir grid (~181k-256k).

Detrend per quarter/sector with wotan biweight, window 0.75-1.0 d for Kepler 30-min M dwarfs and 0.5 d for TESS 200-s/10-min FFIs fitted to 10-min means, break_tolerance=0.5, edge_cutoff=0; clip +3 sigma / -10 sigma only after detrending; set errors from the per-segment point-to-point MAD; then verify the window with 16+ injections per Chopra's recipe.
Reserve holdout quarters/seasons before searching (Kuber: last max(2, ceil(0.25 N)) quarters) and write that split to a manifest; report fixed-ephemeris depth and SNR in the holdout separately.

Run the whole sample inverted (flux -> 2 - flux before cleaning) and, for each candidate, >= 38 quarter/sector scrambles through the identical pipeline and triage; report the real signal against the null distribution of SDE and BLS SNR instead of quoting white-noise FAPs; expect BLS depth-SNR ~10-12 from noise on a 45k-point Kepler LC searched over 500k periods.

Measure candidate depths with Chopra's matched-processing control boxes (40 off-transit phases each re-detrended with that phase masked) and Kuber's local-baseline per-event fits with 24-64 phase controls; require max single-event contribution < 0.5 and consistent odd/even and null secondary.

Vet every survivor with LEO-Vetter compute_flux_metrics + check_thresholds (star dict needs rad, e_rad, mass, e_mass, Teff, e_Teff, rho, u1, u2, id, tic, ra, dec, raDegrees, decDegrees, planetData) and require MES >= 10 for shallow signals, per eumemic's calibration; add exovetter ModShift/Sweet/OddEven as a cross-check.

Fit survivors with batman + emcee using supersample_factor=7 and exp_time=1765.464/86400 d for Kepler LC (or the TESS FFI exposure), a TIC stellar-density prior and a dilution term; report rho_star from the fit against the catalogue value.

Localise the source with per-event, per-pixel local-baseline box fits stacked over all quarters plus lightkurve.prf.KeplerPRF templates at each Gaia position (Kuber's pixel_localize.py) for Kepler, and transit-diffImage / LEO-Vetter pixel_vetting with per-sector centroid F-tests for TESS; do not rely on single-quarter in/out difference images (SNR 0.4 here) or on KBONUS CENTROID columns.

Orchestrate with ProcessPoolExecutor (4 workers, OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL threads = 1, one .npz per star, per-star JSON keyed by input SHA-256 and pipeline_version, imap_unordered chunksize 1); budget ~10 s/star/core for the fast semi-coherent tier (overnight: up to ~10k stars) and move coherent full-grid BLS / TLS-on-everything / TRICERATOPS for > 1k stars to a cloud box (~8,000-12,000 core-hours per 100k Kepler stars at coherent-BLS cost).

Keep disk under control: parse KBONUS FITS (8.4 MB each) to npz (1.4 MB) and delete the FITS, keeping URL + SHA-256 in the manifest; fetch TPFs (1.7 MB/quarter) and TESScut cutouts (3 MB per 30-min sector, ~9x for 200-s sectors) only for candidates.
open_questions: TLS 2.0 changed results in 10 of its 18 bug fixes and the default backend 'fused-pl' is an approximation (2% template deviation); nobody has yet published a re-calibrated SDE-vs-FAP table for TLS 2 on red-noise Kepler/TESS data, and the raw BUGLOG.md could not be fetched (404) to list the exact changes.

The measured wall-clock costs (BLS 150-440 s per Kepler star, TLS 100-200 s) were taken while other agents loaded the 4 vCPUs (load average 5-13); the clean single-core numbers should be re-measured on an idle box before sizing a cloud run.

eumemic's semi-coherent/stack-slide BLS misses ~15% of weak signals that the coherent search finds (18 vs 4 exclusive detections); the right trade-off for Kepler 13-quarter light curves (90-d blocks) was not re-measured here and should be set by injection-recovery on the actual target sample.

Whether exoplanet 0.6.0 works with PyMC 6.3.2 (and exoplanet-core 0.4.0) is unverified; if PyMC-based fitting is wanted, test in a separate venv or use juliet/dynesty, which installed and imported cleanly.

psfmachine (needed to re-extract PSF photometry from Kepler TPFs the way Kepler Bonus did) does not install on Python 3.13 because of its pandas 1.5.3 pin; a Python 3.11 venv was not built or tested here.

ExoMiner's container may run on CPU (amd64/arm64 images) but its documentation does not state hardware requirements, and the pipeline only scores SPOC TCEs; whether the Keras model can be fed a home-made TCE record was not tested.

LDTk's PHOENIX download size and the exact Claret table versions behind TLS's catalog_info were not verified; limb darkening for a 3,600 K M dwarf in the Kepler band should be cross-checked between the two before publication.

Kuber's KBONUS flux choice (per-quarter FLUX = corrected PSF flux) versus PSF_FLAT_FLUX or SAP_FLUX changes the measured depth (1438 vs 2165-2348 ppm in his notes); the dilution/aperture systematics of KBONUS PSF photometry for 7-arcsec blends are not characterised in the Kepler Bonus paper and need an injection test on neighbour TPFs.
